title: Capacity Fairness Canvas and Rapid Prioritization Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, teams oscillate between over-committing to ambitious OKRs and protective under-commitment that starves cross-functional initiatives. Current cycle planning artifacts focus on absolute slices and surge lanes but lack a simple, repeatable fairness ledger and a fast path to reprioritization that engineering, design, and PMs can operate in 30 minutes during weekly cadence.

Goals: 1) Create a Capacity Fairness Canvas to allocate baseline capacity across initiatives, enabling transparent trade-offs. 2) Define a Rapid Prioritization Protocol (RPP) used to make scope cuts and temporary reassignments within a single cycle with minimal ceremony. 3) Pilot the approach with two product squads and the platform team in 2026-Q2.

Deliverables: 1) Canvas template (Confluence + printable one-pager). 2) RPP checklist and decision matrix (triage triggers, guardrails, roles). 3) Lightweight ledger spreadsheet and example entries for skill shadowing and temporary reassignments. 4) Pilot report with simulation of capacity under three stress scenarios and recommended rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canvas template accepted by at least two PM leads and one Eng manager.
- RPP used in at least two mid-cycle cuts with decision logs recorded.
- Pilot report shows less than 15% delivery regression on committed buyer-facing work when fair reserve policy is applied.
- Minimal tooling changes: ledger implemented as Google Sheet + console link; no infra changes required for pilot.
decision_log:
2026-03-03 | PM sync: choose points-based baseline (team velocity * 0.8) + 10% cross-team reserve. Agreed by exec PMs. | Aisha P.
2026-03-07 | Design and Eng feedback: require skill-tagging on ledger entries, add emergency fallback lane (2 FTE-equivalent). | Luca H.
2026-03-09 | Scope-cut threshold: any initiative with 'confidence' <= 40% and dependencies impacted qualifies for fast reprioritization. | Decision: implement RPP checklists and runbook. | Emily K. (Dir Eng)
implementation_notes:
- Canvas fields: initiative, OKR alignment, baseline capacity points, required skills, earliest unblock date, fallback lane indicator.
- Ledger rows: date, owner, from-squad, to-squad, FTE-equivalent, reason, expected duration, rollback condition, linked GH PR/DOC.
- Scoring: compute 'fairness delta' = (allocated_points - expected_velocity)/team_size_normalized. Use this to surface candidate reassignments.
- Pilot automation: a tiny script (one-off) will aggregate weekly velocity and populate ledger suggestions; stored as Google Sheet and a companion summary in Console -> Cycle Insights.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (this ticket): finalize canvas and RPP checklist; prepare pilot ledger and Confluence doc.
Phase 1 (pilot weeks 1-4): run with Platform + Squad A + Squad B; document every RPP activation.
Phase 2 (analysis week 5): measure delivery, quality, and morale signals; iterate canvas.
Phase 3 (scale): if pilot meets acceptance criteria, publish runbook and add a light UX flow inside Console for cycle leads to view ledger entries. Target: release in cycle-planning-tooling-2026.04.
risks:
- Teams may feel punished by fairness allocations; mitigations include explicit opt-ins for skill shadowing and guaranteed rollback conditions.
- Overhead: initial bookkeeping could be burdensome; mitigation: keep ledger entries to one-line events and automate suggestions.
- Cross-team dependencies may still cause hidden blockers; mitigate by requiring 'earliest_unblock_date' and dependency owner in the canvas.
- Measurement noise: velocity fluctuations can skew allocations; mitigation: smooth with 3-cycle rolling average.
